title: The Gilded Age
tagline: A fortune that shaped an era — and the questions it could never answer.

scenes.text: Pittsburgh, 1890. Smoke blackens the sky above the steel mills. Carnegie, Rockefeller, Morgan — the titans of American industry are building fortunes that dwarf the GDP of most nations. Andrew Mellon watches, calculates, and invests.

scenes.speaker: Andrew Mellon
scenes.text: Capital is not evil. Capital is energy. Channel it correctly — fund the right industries, back the right men — and it lifts everyone. Channel it wrongly and you get monopoly, exploitation, and revolution.

challenge.fact: Andrew Mellon served as Treasury Secretary under Harding, Coolidge, and Hoover (1921–1932) — the longest tenure since Alexander Hamilton. He oversaw the Roaring Twenties boom and the beginning of the Great Depression, for which he was blamed.

params.title: Andrew Mellon served as US Treasury
params.intro: Andrew Mellon served as US Treasury Secretary under three consecutive presidents.

challenge.instruction: Andrew Mellon served as US Treasury Secretary under three consecutive presidents. Wire the gates until the circuit agrees with the table on every row.

scenes.text: Mellon served as Treasury Secretary through three presidencies. His deep tax cuts in the 1920s fueled the economic boom — and critics say contributed to the inequality that preceded the Great Crash of 1929.

challenge.instruction: Mellon's National Gallery of Art is a masterpiece of architectural geometry. Calculate the space diagonal of this cubic gallery room.
challenge.fact: Mellon donated his art collection and $15 million to build Washington's National Gallery of Art — one of the greatest acts of private cultural philanthropy in American history. His collection included Raphaels, Rembrandts, and van Eycks bought from the Hermitage.

scenes.speaker: Andrew Mellon
scenes.text: I will give the National Gallery to the people of the United States — the most significant collection of art ever assembled, for a country that did not always believe it deserved such things. Wealth must eventually serve beauty.

challenge.instruction: Andrew Mellon faces the Senate with his Revenue Act, proposing to cut the top income tax rate from 73% to 25%. Win enough votes to pass it.
challenge.fact: Mellon's Revenue Acts of 1921, 1924, and 1926 cut the top marginal rate from 73% to 25%. Tax revenues rose during the 1920s boom, but the same policies concentrated wealth so severely that the Depression proved catastrophic. Mellon advised Hoover to 'liquidate labour, liquidate stocks' in 1929 — advice that deepened the crisis.

challenge.instruction: Trade Carnegie Steel shares over 8 rounds of market events. Reach the target portfolio to win.
challenge.fact: Carnegie Steel's rise mirrored the Gilded Age: astonishing wealth creation alongside brutal labour conditions. The 1892 Homestead Strike left seven dead and fatally damaged Carnegie's public image, despite his later philanthropic legacy.

challenge.instruction: Bid on industrial-era assets at the Gilded Age estate sale. Secure your target investments wisely.
challenge.fact: The Gilded Age saw explosive growth in auction houses and financial markets as railroads, steel, and electricity transformed the American economy.
